units.title: Phobia
units.intro: Grammar: the third conditional for imagining a different past.

cards.title: Conditional type 3
rule: **Form:** *If + past perfect, would have + past participle.* *If she **had studied**, she **would have passed**.*

**Meaning:** an imaginary past: the condition did **not** happen, so the result did not happen either. It is often used for regrets: *If I **had known** about my fear of heights, I **wouldn’t have climbed** the tower.*
Could have / might have can replace would have: *If we had left earlier, we **might have caught** the bus.*

examples.text: If he had trained, he would have won.
If he would have trained, he would have won.
examples.fix: If he had trained, he would have won.

examples.text: If I had seen you, I would have said hello.

cards.pattern: If + had + pp, would have + pp

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "If he would have trained, he would have won."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** **Form:** *If + past perfect, would have + past participle.* *If she **had studied**, she **would have passed**.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "If he would have trained, he would have won." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "If he had trained, he would have won."

**Check:** **Meaning:** an imaginary past: the condition did **not** happen, so the result did not happen either. It is often used for regrets: *If I **had known** about my fear of heights, I **wouldn’t have climbed** the tower.*

cards.answer: If he had trained, he would have won.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle, for imaginary past situations and regrets. Might have or could have show possibility.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: If you had gone to Massawa last year, ________________?

options.B: what sites may you have visited
options.C: what sites will you have visited
options.D: what sites would you have visited

cards.why: This is a Third Conditional question about an imaginary situation in the past. The structure is **If + Past Perfect, would have + Past Participle**. Therefore, 'would you have visited' is the correct completion.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Had I known you were at home, _________.

options.B: I would have ring you earlier
options.C: I would have rung you earlier

cards.why: 'Had I known' is an inverted form of 'If I had known' (Type 3 Conditional). The result clause must use 'would have + past participle (rung)'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Abraham didn’t realize that Ruth was in hospital. If he ____ she was in hospital, he ____ to visit her.
cards.why: This is a **Third Conditional** sentence, used to talk about unreal situations in the past. Structure: If + Past Perfect (had known), ... would have + Past Participle (would have gone).
